text:
Michael: quick follow-up from the conditional-fallback RFC — proposal for a thin orchestration shim that composes simple policies (latency, error-rate, token-cost) rather than one huge state machine.
Sara: curious — what's the sig for these policies? runtime hook?
Michael: idea is small pluggable adapters with a 3-field contract: canHandle(request-meta) -> score, decision(request-meta, probe) -> action. action enums: ALLOW, THROTTLE, SWITCH_VARIANT, FALLBACK.
Devin: so adapters score then a combiner picks winner? sounds like scoring + arbitration. how do we avoid oscillation when two adapters fight?
Priya: we need hysteresis window + token-weighted smoothing. cheap approach: prefer last-stable-variant if scores close and tie-break by tenant-priority.
Michael: agreed. tie-break rules + debounce timer handled by shim. Also a circuit-breaker fallback: if runtime reports degraded-qps for Xs and error-rate > threshold, immediate SWITCH_VARIANT to safer model.
Sara: question on sticky sessions: many customers rely on KV cache warmup for quality. if we SWITCH_VARIANT mid-session, can degrade outputs. how to expose opt-outs?
Devin: we can add session-affinity policy: adapter can emit KEEP_SESSION tag that forces only non-destructive actions (THROTTLE or DELAY) for that session id. default is stateless.
Priya: telemetry — we must emit decision-reason + pre/post-latency + sample output hash for quality regression detection. ops-bot should tag any auto-switch with incident if user-rate drops > 2% for 5m.
ops-bot: noted — will create alert channel badge for auto-switch events when flagged by telemetry rules.
Michael: tradeoffs: complexity vs safety. Benefits: localized policies per-route, easier testing. Costs: more surface area to configure and maintain, potential for inconsistent behavior across runtimes.
Sara: long-term: consider a declarative rollout DSL that compiles to these adapters, so SRE/product use same surface. short-term: shipping shim with 3 adapters: latency-threshold, error-rate, cost-safety.
Devin: prototype suggestions: run shim as a sidecar in Dedicated and a gateway plugin in Hosted. sidecar gets richer signals (GPU metrics, KV cache hits). plugin has coarser signals but faster path.
Priya: we need a safety net mode: 'observe-only' where decisions are logged but not acted on, to evaluate false positives. put that behind a feature flag per-tenant.
Michael: testing plan: chaos test that injects 10-50% slowdown for model-A, ensure SWITCH_VARIANT and then warm-up vs KEEP_SESSION behavior. add unit tests for arbitration tie-breaks.
Sara: config proto sketch (very rough):
```
policy {
 name: "latency_threshold"
 params { p90_ms: 120 }
 action: SWITCH_VARIANT
}
combiner { mode: "highest_score" tie_break: "last_stable" }
```
Devin: a couple of nitpicks: specify evaluation window (count-based vs time-based) and a minimum-sample threshold to avoid acting on noise.
Priya: owner suggestions: runtime team owns shim implementation; eng-platform owns DSL + rollout UI; eng-sre owns default policy sets + alerts.
Michael: ok can we get +1 from runtime and eng-platform on ownership and shipping sequence? planning: 2-week prototype -> 4-week dogfood -> opt-in tenants -> gradual enable.
Sara: +1 from eng-platform on DSL/UX ownership.
Devin: +1 from runtime for sidecar prototype, leaning to conservative defaults.
Priya: +1 from SRE for alerting & observe-only path.
Michael: great — I'll draft an implementation RFC with the adapter contract, sample configs, and the test plan. please comment on the RFC when I post it (will link in this thread).
Sara: minor ask: document cost impact estimate for extra telemetry + decision calls (tokens and CPU). ops-bot can we get a quick cost delta calc?
ops-bot: I can produce a baseline report if you ping me with sample qps and retention window.
Michael: thanks. tagging follow-ups: @Devin please do the sidecar perf sketch; @Sara please prototype DSL toy; @Priya please draft alert rules.
Priya: will do.
Devin: starting sketch today.
Sara: will mock DSL by EOD.
Michael: awesome — closing loop. will post RFC link shortly. :rocket:
